cards.title: Navigate and inspect files
cards.code:
pwd
ls -lah
cd "my project"
cards.explanation: Quote paths containing spaces; cd changes the current shell directory.

cards.title: Find files by name
cards.code: find src -type f -name "*.ts"
cards.explanation: Quote glob patterns so find receives them unchanged.

cards.title: Search source text
cards.code: rg -n --glob "*.rs" "TODO|FIXME" src
cards.explanation: rg is an optional tool; quote regexes and globs.

cards.title: Filter and count a stream
cards.code: git ls-files | sort | head -n 20
cards.explanation: A pipe sends standard output to the next command; uniq only combines adjacent duplicates.

cards.title: Redirect output and errors
cards.code:
pnpm test > test.log 2>&1
tail -n 40 test.log
cards.explanation: The > operator overwrites a file; >> appends. Redirection order matters.

cards.title: Set an environment variable
cards.code:
export APP_ENV=development
APP_ENV=test cargo test
cards.explanation: Assignment before a command applies to that command only in POSIX shells.

cards.title: Quote paths and expansions
cards.code:
project="my project"
printf "%s\n" "$project"
cards.explanation: Double quotes preserve spaces while allowing expansion; single quotes suppress expansion.

cards.title: Run commands on success
cards.code: test -f Cargo.toml && cargo check
cards.explanation: && runs after success; || runs after a nonzero exit status.

cards.title: Process matching files
cards.code:
for file in src/*.rs; do
  test -f "$file" || continue
  printf "%s\n" "$file"
done
cards.explanation: Quote expanded file names. Unmatched globs may remain literal in POSIX shells.

cards.title: Review local Git changes
cards.code:
git status --short
git diff --stat
git diff -- src
cards.explanation: git diff shows unstaged changes; --staged shows the index.

cards.title: Create a feature branch
cards.code:
git switch -c feat/health-check
git branch --show-current
cards.explanation: -c creates a branch from the current commit; an existing branch needs no -c.

cards.title: Inspect recent commits
cards.code:
git log --oneline -n 10
git show --stat HEAD
cards.explanation: HEAD identifies the current commit.

cards.title: Check Rust code
cards.code:
cargo check --all-targets
cargo build --release
cards.explanation: Run inside a Cargo project; check skips final code generation.

cards.title: Run Rust tests
cards.code:
cargo test --workspace
cargo test parse_config -- --nocapture
cards.explanation: Arguments after -- go to the test harness.

cards.title: Run a Rust program
cards.code: cargo run --bin server -- --port 8080
cards.explanation: Arguments after -- go to the executable.

cards.title: Format and lint Rust
cards.code:
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cards.explanation: rustfmt and clippy components must be installed; --check avoids modifying files.

cards.title: Run Go tests
cards.code:
go test ./...
go test -race -run TestParse ./...
cards.explanation: ./... includes packages below the current module; race testing needs a supported platform/toolchain.

cards.title: Build or run Go
cards.code:
go build ./...
go run ./cmd/server
cards.explanation: Run from a Go module; go run compiles and executes a main package.

cards.title: Format and vet Go
cards.code:
gofmt -l .
go vet ./...
cards.explanation: gofmt -l lists files; -w and go fmt rewrite them.

cards.title: Maintain Go dependencies
cards.code:
go mod tidy
go mod download
cards.explanation: tidy updates go.mod and go.sum; dependency operations can access the network.

cards.title: Install JavaScript dependencies
cards.code:
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
# npm alternative, with package-lock.json:
npm ci
cards.explanation: Use the project package manager; frozen installs fail when manifests and lockfiles disagree.

cards.title: Run JavaScript project scripts
cards.code:
pnpm run build
pnpm test
# npm alternative:
npm run build
cards.explanation: Script names and argument handling depend on the project and package manager.

cards.title: Type-check TypeScript
cards.code:
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
# npm alternative, with TypeScript installed locally:
npx --no-install tsc --noEmit
cards.explanation: Install TypeScript in the project; --noEmit checks without generating files.

cards.title: Choose a Node runtime
cards.code:
nvm use
node --version
pnpm --version
cards.explanation: nvm must be installed and loaded; nvm use reads .nvmrc when no version is given.

cards.title: Inspect an HTTP response
cards.code: curl --fail --show-error --include http://localhost:8080/health
cards.explanation: --fail returns a failure status for HTTP errors; --include prints response headers.

cards.title: Inspect running processes
cards.code:
ps -ef
pgrep -af "my-server"
cards.explanation: Options vary across platforms; these examples target Linux developer shells.

cards.title: Discover AWS CLI commands locally
cards.code:
aws --version
aws help
aws s3 help
aws ec2 describe-instances help
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Local help needs no AWS account; Unix installations may need groff/less to display it.

cards.title: Sign in to a development AWS profile
cards.code:
aws configure sso --profile dev
aws sso login --profile dev
aws sts get-caller-identity --profile dev --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Requires your organization’s SSO start URL, region, account and role. Configuration changes local AWS files; confirm the returned account before further work.

cards.title: Check AWS profile and region selection
cards.code:
aws configure list-profiles
aws configure list --profile dev
aws sts get-caller-identity --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. List profile names and configuration sources, then verify identity. Do not publish configuration output.

cards.title: Filter running EC2 instances into a table
cards.code:
aws ec2 describe-instances --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 \
  --filters Name=instance-state-name,Values=running \
  --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Id:InstanceId,Type:InstanceType,IP:PrivateIpAddress}' \
  --output table --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. The EC2 filter is server-side; the JMESPath object selects columns locally. This is a read-only inventory request.

cards.title: Read a bounded page of AWS Lambda functions
cards.code:
aws lambda list-functions --profile dev --max-items 10 --output json --no-cli-pager
# If the response includes NextToken, paste it into the next call:
aws lambda list-functions --profile dev --max-items 10 \
  --starting-token 'PASTE_NEXT_TOKEN' --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Replace PASTE_NEXT_TOKEN with the returned CLI NextToken; pagination tokens are opaque and should not be constructed.

cards.title: List and download a build artifact from S3
cards.code:
aws s3 ls s3://example-build-artifacts/releases/ --profile dev
aws s3 cp s3://example-build-artifacts/releases/app.zip ./app.zip --profile dev
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Replace the example bucket and key with resources you can read. The download writes or overwrites ./app.zip.

cards.title: Preview uploading a local S3 artifact
cards.code:
aws s3 cp ./app.zip s3://example-build-artifacts/releases/app.zip --profile dev --dryrun
# Remove --dryrun only after checking the destination.
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Requires a local file and access to the destination bucket. Removing --dryrun writes an object and can replace an existing key.

cards.title: Create a short-lived S3 download link
cards.code: aws s3 presign s3://example-build-artifacts/releases/app.zip --profile dev --expires-in 900
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Creates a bearer download URL lasting up to 15 minutes, bounded by credential lifetime. Treat the URL as sensitive.

cards.title: Preview syncing static assets to S3
cards.code:
aws s3 sync ./dist/ s3://example-static-site/assets/ --profile dev \
  --exclude '*' --include '*.css' --include '*.js' --no-follow-symlinks --dryrun
# Review the preview, then remove --dryrun to upload.
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Requires a local dist directory. Includes only CSS/JS after excluding all files; leaves extra destination objects intact.

cards.title: Inspect an S3 artifact before downloading
cards.code:
aws s3api head-object --bucket example-build-artifacts --key releases/app.zip --profile dev \
  --query '{Bytes:ContentLength,Modified:LastModified,Type:ContentType}' --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Reads metadata only; requires permission to access the object. Bucket/key names are illustrative.

cards.title: List S3 object keys as structured JSON
cards.code:
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket example-build-artifacts --prefix releases/ --profile dev \
  --query 'Contents[].{Key:Key,Size:Size}' --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Uses automatic pagination and a local projection; an empty prefix may have no Contents field.

cards.title: Find EC2 instances tagged for development
cards.code:
aws ec2 describe-instances --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 \
  --filters Name=tag:Environment,Values=dev \
  --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Id:InstanceId,State:State.Name,IP:PrivateIpAddress}' \
  --output table --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Read-only inventory by tag; change the tag key/value to match your environment.

cards.title: Wait for a known EC2 instance to become running
cards.code:
if aws ec2 wait instance-running --instance-ids i-0123456789abcdef0 --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2; then
  printf "Instance is running\n"
else
  printf "Wait failed or timed out\n" >&2
fi
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Replace the instance ID. This only polls state; it does not launch or start the instance.

cards.title: Inspect an application role and managed policies
cards.code:
aws iam get-role --role-name example-app-role --profile dev \
  --query 'Role.{Arn:Arn,Trust:AssumeRolePolicyDocument}' --output json --no-cli-pager
aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name example-app-role --profile dev --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Replace the role name. These read-only calls show trust and attached managed policies, not a complete effective-permissions calculation.

cards.title: Follow recent Lambda logs
cards.code:
aws logs tail /aws/lambda/example-handler --since 10m --follow --format short \
  --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2
# Press Ctrl-C to stop following.
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Reads from an existing log group. Replace the group name and avoid sharing sensitive log contents.

cards.title: Find error events in an application log group
cards.code:
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/lambda/example-handler \
  --filter-pattern '"ERROR"' --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 \
  --query 'events[].{Time:timestamp,Message:message}' --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. The quoted ERROR term is a CloudWatch Logs filter. No time bounds means the service searches all retained events.

cards.title: Invoke a development Lambda with a JSON event
cards.code:
printf '%s\n' '{"action":"healthcheck"}' > event.json
aws lambda invoke --function-name example-handler --payload fileb://event.json \
  --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 --no-cli-pager response.json
cat response.json
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Writes event.json and response.json locally. Use a development function with a safe test event; inspect invocation metadata for FunctionError as well as the response body.

cards.title: Inspect a Lambda runtime and timeout
cards.code:
aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name example-handler --profile dev \
  --query '{Runtime:Runtime,Memory:MemorySize,Timeout:Timeout,State:State}' --output table --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Read-only configuration inspection; the projection avoids displaying environment variables.

cards.title: Inspect a CloudFormation stack and recent events
cards.code:
aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name example-app-dev --profile dev \
  --query 'Stacks[0].{Status:StackStatus,Outputs:Outputs}' --output json --no-cli-pager
aws cloudformation describe-stack-events --stack-name example-app-dev --profile dev \
  --max-items 10 --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Read-only status, outputs and events for an existing stack; outputs may include sensitive application details.

cards.title: Prepare a CloudFormation change set for review
cards.code:
aws cloudformation deploy --template-file ./template.yaml --stack-name example-app-dev \
  --parameter-overrides Environment=dev --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 \
  --no-execute-changeset
# Use the printed change-set ARN to inspect it before execution.
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Requires a real template and permissions. Creates a change set (and possibly an initial review-state stack), but does not execute infrastructure changes.

cards.title: Read one DynamoDB item by its complete key
cards.code:
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name example-orders \
  --key '{"PK":{"S":"ORDER#123"},"SK":{"S":"META"}}' \
  --consistent-read --profile dev --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Assumes string partition/sort keys named PK/SK. Replace names and values to match the table schema; this consumes read capacity.

cards.title: Query DynamoDB orders for a customer
cards.code:
aws dynamodb query --table-name example-orders \
  --key-condition-expression '#pk = :customer' \
  --expression-attribute-names '{"#pk":"PK"}' \
  --expression-attribute-values '{":customer":{"S":"CUSTOMER#123"}}' \
  --profile dev --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Assumes PK is the string partition key. Uses typed JSON and an attribute-name alias; reads only the matching partition.

cards.title: Read a non-secret development parameter
cards.code:
aws ssm get-parameter --name /example/dev/api-base-url --profile dev \
  --query 'Parameter.Value' --output text --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Use a non-sensitive String parameter. For SecureString add --with-decryption only when plaintext output is appropriate.

cards.title: Connect to an SSM-managed development instance
cards.code: aws ssm start-session --target i-0123456789abcdef0 --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Replace the instance ID; requires Session Manager plugin and a configured managed instance. Opens an interactive remote session.

cards.title: Inspect secret rotation without displaying its value
cards.code:
aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id example/dev/database --profile dev \
  --query '{Name:Name,Rotation:RotationEnabled,Changed:LastChangedDate}' --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Reads secret metadata without fetching SecretString or SecretBinary.

cards.title: Retrieve a development secret in a private terminal
cards.code:
# Prints plaintext: use only in a private terminal, never a shared log.
aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id example/dev/database --profile dev \
  --version-stage AWSCURRENT --query SecretString --output text --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Requires a string-valued secret and decrypt permission. Prints the current plaintext value; applications should normally retrieve it through an SDK.

cards.title: Authenticate Docker to a development ECR registry
cards.code:
aws ecr get-login-password --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 | \
  docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 123456789012.dkr.ecr.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Requires Docker; replace the sample account ID with your registry account. Saves Docker credentials without printing the password.

cards.title: Inspect image tags and push times in ECR
cards.code:
aws ecr describe-images --repository-name example-app --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 \
  --query 'imageDetails[].{Tags:imageTags,Pushed:imagePushedAt,Digest:imageDigest}' --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Read-only repository inventory; untagged images may have no Tags value.

cards.title: Inspect ECS desired and running task counts
cards.code:
aws ecs describe-services --cluster example-dev --services example-api --profile dev \
  --region ap-southeast-2 --query '{Services:services[].{Name:serviceName,Desired:desiredCount,Running:runningCount,Deployments:deployments},Failures:failures}' \
  --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Read-only service status; inspect Failures if the service or cluster is not found.

cards.title: Preview kubectl configuration for an EKS cluster
cards.code:
aws eks describe-cluster --name example-dev --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 \
  --query cluster.status --output text --no-cli-pager
aws eks update-kubeconfig --name example-dev --alias example-dev \
  --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 --dry-run
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Reads cluster data and prints kubeconfig without writing it. Remove --dry-run only when ready to change local kubectl context.

cards.title: List CloudWatch alarms currently in ALARM state
cards.code:
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --state-value ALARM --profile dev --region ap-southeast-2 \
  --query '{Metric:MetricAlarms[].{Name:AlarmName,Reason:StateReason},Composite:CompositeAlarms[].{Name:AlarmName,Reason:StateReason}}' \
  --output json --no-cli-pager
cards.explanation: AWS CLI v2. Read-only alarm status. Composite alarms may require broader DescribeAlarms permission.
